articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a casual 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Just another Tuesday in Redmond's perpetual game of security whack-a-mole.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vuln is getting exploited in the wild with ransomware demands already rolling in. Millions of sites potentially pwned because hosting infrastructure is apparently made of hopes and dreams.

articles.title: cPanel drops patches for exploited authentication bypass zero-day
articles.summary: Watchtowr drops their legendary snark on the cPanel authentication bypass CVE-2026-41940. When they say 'the internet is falling down,' they're not being dramatic—they're being accurate.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence hackers are mass-harvesting Microsoft Office tokens through compromised routers. Because why hack individual users when you can automate the apocalypse?

articles.title: Polymarket Rejects Data Breach Claims as Hacker Alleges 300K Records Stolen
articles.summary: A 15-year-old allegedly pwned France's entire ID agency and tried selling millions of citizens' data on the dark web. Gen Z strikes again with their casual approach to nation-state-level breaches.

articles.title: Hackers are actively exploiting a bug in cPanel, used by millions of websites | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sri Lanka loses over $3 million in two separate cyber incidents while recovering from debt crisis. When you're already broke and hackers decide to kick you while you're down.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: FOIA requests are exposing ALPR surveillance abuse, so naturally states want to block public access to the data. Transparency is only good when it doesn't reveal how dystopian we've become.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's new anti-VPN law goes live next week, because nothing says 'freedom' like criminalizing basic privacy tools. Watch VPN usage surge faster than a DDoS attack.

articles.title: Trump Bulldozed a 1,000-Year-Old Archeological Site to Make Room for a Second Border Wall
articles.summary: FBI reassigned 9,000 agents—a quarter of their workforce—to hunt immigrants under Trump's deportation push. National security takes a backseat to political theater once again.

articles.title: Best of Both Sides | iMessage from Claude Mythos: It’s too late for regulation, AI needs slowing down
articles.summary: Two cybersecurity professionals get 4-year sentences for BlackCat ransomware attacks. When the defenders become the attackers, you know the industry's moral compass is completely fucked.
